docs.summary: Everything Aperture can report about an image without decoding its pixels. Produced by [`Identify`](#api~Prowl.Aperture.Image~Identify), which reads only as much of the file as the header occupies, so it stays cheap on large files and on files that would fail to decode.

docs.summary: Height of the primary image in pixels.
Bits per colour channel as stored in the file, before any conversion.
Number of stored channels, counting alpha.
Whether the file carries per pixel transparency.
Whether samples cover a range beyond the unit interval and want a float target.
How stored samples relate to colour before conversion.
The layout a decode produces when [`TargetPixelFormat`](#api~Prowl.Aperture.DecodeOptions~TargetPixelFormat) is null.
Number of frames, images or icon entries in the container. One for a plain still image, zero when the count cannot be known without a full parse.
Whether [`FrameCount`](#api~Prowl.Aperture.ImageInfo~FrameCount) frames form an animation rather than independent images.
Number of stored mipmap levels, one when the format has no mip chain.
The transform needed to bring stored pixels into display order.
Horizontal resolution in dots per inch, zero when the file does not say.
Vertical resolution in dots per inch, zero when the file does not say.
Which camera raw flavour this is, for [`Raw`](#api~Prowl.Aperture.ImageFormat~Raw) files.

Width of the region the file asks to be displayed, or zero where it carries no clean aperture. [`Width`](#api~Prowl.Aperture.ImageInfo~Width) stays the stored frame, since that is the buffer a decode produces, and cropping to this rectangle is the caller's choice.
Height of the region the file asks to be displayed, zero when it has no clean aperture.
Name of the compression the file uses, in the format's own vocabulary, for example "Progressive", "Deflate", "PIZ", "BC7" or "RLE". Null when there is nothing meaningful to say.
Total pixels in the primary image, as a long so the multiply cannot overflow.
